newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing a July global trade deficit of 1.23 billion stg and an August non-EU trade deficit of 499 million stg.
The Reuters consensus forecast was for a visible trade deficit of 775 million stg in July and a non-EU trade shortfall of 750 million stg in August.
"The whole-world figure for July looks somewhat worse than expected...a little bit worrying."
"But on the other hand, looking at the more up to date August figures for the rest of the world excluding Europe, the deficit there is actually somewhat smaller than people were looking for."

"We were rather surprised by the weakness of imports by the UK from Europe. Our suspicion is that UK activity is picking up quite sharply at the moment and we would expect to see some strong pickup in imports from our European partners over the next few months. The overall trend is very flat. The global balance is averaging about one to 1-1/4 billion per month, so we're not moving out of the trend. It doesn't really help the Chancellor with his case for lower interest rates. I think we're still looking at the opposite scenario."

"UK trade data mixed, with the July global shortfall larger than expected but the August non-EU deficit surprisingly small. Net impact probably small, but would see net export demand as marginally positive. Performance versus the non-EU countries particularly promising last month, with exports surprisingly robust, albeit from a weaker revised July volume level. Global picture shows a widening in the shortfall with the EU in July, but with exports down and imports up, almost certainly says more about the relative performance of UK domestic demand vs EU demand than anything to do with stg being over-valued."
